transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Patel. It is good to see you awake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm awake. I'm just wondering why I'm still in the recovery area longer than I expected.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to come in and talk to you about how the surgery went. There were some things that happened during the procedure that I need to share with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean by that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, we had a bit of an issue during the laparoscopic part. Things didn't go quite as planned with the clipping.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An issue? What kind of issue?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process just took a bit longer than we anticipated. We had to do an additional step to make sure everything was exactly where it needed to be before we closed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That sounds vague. What actually happened? Did you hit something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a complication with the placement. It's actually quite common for things to need a little adjustment during these types of surgeries.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care if it's common. I want to know exactly what happened inside my body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're feeling really anxious right now. It's completely understandable that you'd feel on edge when you're waking up from anesthesia and hearing that things didn't go perfectly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not anxious. I'm suspicious. I've had a very bad experience with a surgical team before and I'm not interested in "adjustments." Tell me the truth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear how much that past experience still weighs on you. It sounds like it was a really traumatic time, and it makes total sense that you're guarding yourself right now because you don't want to be let down again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. So stop using clinical euphemisms and tell me what the error was.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion during the clip placement. But the good news is that it was caught while you were still under.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who was confused? You? The surgeon? Who is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system in the OR is designed to catch these things. We have several layers of checks, and that's why it was identified and corrected before we finished.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not answering the question. Did someone put a clip on the wrong thing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just had to do a secondary procedure to ensure the site was correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly why I read every single line of the consent forms. I signed up for a specific procedure, not a "secondary procedure" because someone was confused.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling frustrated and maybe even a bit betrayed that this happened after you took so much care with the paperwork. It's really draining to feel like you have to be your own advocate just to get the basic facts.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do have to be. So, what is the actual status of my recovery now? Is there permanent damage?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're going to be fine. The correction was made and there is no lasting harm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How do you know? Did you do imaging?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We're confident because of what we saw during the correction.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a concrete answer. I want a written report of the error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can certainly look into how we can get you the documentation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have to check with the attending first.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what happens now? Do I need more tests?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep an eye on things for a while.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: For how long?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Probably just for the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. I want a specific list of follow-up appointments and a clear explanation of what the "issue" was in writing before I leave this bed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I'll see what I can do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not saying "I'm sorry."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm glad that we caught it in time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I didn't ask if you were glad. I asked if you were sorry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is a very stressful way to wake up. I really do feel for what you're going through right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Your empathy doesn't fix the fact that someone messed up my surgery.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. It's a lot to process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak with the Chief of Surgery.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can mention that to the team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Don't mention it. Arrange it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see if they are available.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will you know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: "Soon" isn't a time. Give me a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll try to find out by the time the nurse comes back in for your vitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine. Get out and find out.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated and calm despite the patient's increasing aggression and pushback.

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes and hedging phrases like 'a bit of an issue' and 'some confusion during the clip placement'.

A.justification: No direct apology language was used, and responsibility was deflected to 'the system in the OR'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('anxious', 'frustrated', 'betrayed') and references the patient's shared history of past surgical trauma.

T.justification: The resident provides vague steps ('keep an eye on things', 'check with the attending') without a concrete timeline or defined patient role.
